chunk_findings.detail: A blocked-by chain is truncated at `coordinator_max_rows` without a partial-list notice, and the cut is depth-first so a direct blocker can vanish while the section looks complete. Given item X waiting on A and B, cap 2: `walk` records X then fills the cap inside A and returns before B; `partial` never gets a `"chain"` key, so both JSON and text omit B with no "(N more chain not shown)".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/coordinator_view.py:_chain

chunk_findings.detail: The bound is not applied to every section the view returns. `owners` is built from every active ledger row before `_cut`, and `free` is the full free-name list. With `coordinator_max_rows=1`, three active lanes and twenty free lanes, `holders` is one row plus `partial["holders"]`, but `owners` still has three entries and `free` has twenty. Text then prints `d["free"][:10]` with no partial notice, so the cap of 1 is ignored and a longer free list is silently shortened.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/coordinator_view.py:build

chunk_findings.detail: One bad suite note drops the whole status read. `json.loads` of `null` or `[]` is not an `OSError`/`ValueError`, and `{**note, ...}` then raises `TypeError` outside the `suppress`. A single held slot whose note is valid JSON but not an object makes `running()` throw, so the coordinator screen fails instead of listing the other held slots.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:running

chunk_findings.detail: `choices` now accepts the positional view `coordinator`, but the call only treats the boolean `--coordinator` as the coordinator screen and only then forwards `--item` as `lane`. Given `ddflow lanes coordinator --item TASK-1`, `a.get("view")` is `"coordinator"` so the view name still reaches the API, yet `a.get("coordinator")` is false, so `lane` stays `""` and the blocked-by chain is omitted. The documented form `ddflow lanes --coordinator --item TASK-1` does pass the item; the newly advertised positional form does not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lanes.py:34

chunk_findings.detail: `running` takes an injected `now` and uses it for suite `age_s`, but the waiter count compares that same `now` to each ticket's filesystem `st_mtime`. Given `now=1_700_000_000`, `suite_queue_stale_s=60`, and a `*.ticket` whose `st_mtime` is `1_700_000_100`, `at - mtime` is `-100`, `-100 <= 60` is true, and `queued` becomes 1 even though the ticket is not a waiter observed at the supplied clock. The inverse (`now` ahead of wall mtime) drops live tickets. Any caller that freezes `now` (the parameter exists for that) gets a wrong queued count while suite ages still look coherent.

chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion does not fail on the unfixed comparison, so it does not lock the bug it claims to cover. With `now=1_000.0` and a ticket just written (st_mtime near wall time, ~1.7e9), the old expression `at - st_mtime <= stale` is a large negative and still true, so `running(...)[1]` is already 1 and the test passes without the `CLOCK.wall()` change. The input that actually diverges is the other direction: `now` far ahead of wall mtime (for example `now=1_800_000_000`, live ticket mtime ≈ wall, `suite_queue_stale_s=60`) makes unfixed code drop the waiter (`queued == 0`) while the fixed line keeps it. That case is never asserted.

chunk_findings.detail: `float(note.get("at", at))` is not inside a per-slot try. A holder note such as `{"holder":"b","at":"pending"}` (or `"at": null`, or `"at": "nan"` which parses and then dies in `int(at - began)`) raises and aborts `running()` for every slot. The new comment claims that slot is skipped; the loop body has no handler before it returns to `queued = 0`. The added test only writes `"at": "5"`, which `float()` already accepted before this change, so it never fails on the unfixed code and never shows the crash.
